questions.prompt: In a grouped frequency table, a continuous class interval is given as $15 \le x < 35$ and has a frequency of $46$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the class width and calculate the frequency density for this class interval.

questions.prompt: A histogram bar representing the class $10 \le y < 25$ has a height corresponding to a frequency density of $3.6$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the frequency represented by this bar.

questions.prompt: A student measures ages rounded to the nearest year. One class interval is recorded as $20 - 34$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: State the exact continuous lower and upper boundaries of this class interval, and state its true class width.

questions.prompt: A histogram is to be drawn for continuous grouped data with unequal class widths.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Explain why frequency density must be plotted on the vertical axis rather than raw frequency.

questions.prompt:
The table below shows cumulative frequencies for test scores of 80 students:
$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Upper class boundary} & 20 & 40 & 70 \\ \hline \text{Cumulative frequency} & 18 & 50 & 80 \\ \hline \end{array}$$
The lower boundary of the first class is 0.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the ordinary class frequencies for the classes $0 \le x < 20$, $20 \le x < 40$, and $40 \le x < 70$.

questions.prompt: On a histogram, a class of width 10 has a frequency density of 2.4 and is drawn as a rectangle of width $2\text{ cm}$ and height $6\text{ cm}$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the area on the paper, in $\text{cm}^2$, that represents a frequency of 1.

questions.prompt:
The table shows the waiting times $t$, in minutes, of 100 passengers at an airport check-in desk:
$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Waiting time } (t\text{ minutes}) & 0 \le t < 10 & 10 \le t < 20 & 20 \le t < 35 & 35 \le t < 50 \\ \hline \text{Frequency} & 22 & 38 & 24 & 16 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the class width and frequency density for each of the four class intervals.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: State the modal class interval, and identify which bar in the histogram has the greatest height.

questions.prompt:
A continuous variable $x$ is recorded to the nearest whole unit in four classes:
$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Recorded class} & 10 - 19 & 20 - 29 & 30 - 44 & 45 - 59 \\ \hline \text{Frequency} & 16 & 25 & 45 & 21 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the continuous class boundaries and the true class width for each class.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the frequency density for each class, and determine the modal class.

questions.prompt:
A completed histogram has four touching bars representing the distribution of time spent exercising by 90 adults.
The histogram features are as follows:
- Bar 1: from 0 to 10 hours, height 2.2
- Bar 2: from 10 to 25 hours, height 3.0
- Bar 3: from 25 to 35 hours, height 1.5
- Bar 4: from 35 to 50 hours, height $h$

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the frequencies represented by Bar 1, Bar 2, and Bar 3.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Given that the total frequency of the distribution is 90, calculate the frequency of Bar 4 and determine the value of $h$.

questions.prompt:
The table below gives the distribution of weekly pocket money $m$, in dollars, for 75 teenagers:
$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Pocket money } (m\text{ dollars}) & 0 \le m < 10 & 10 \le m < 20 & 20 \le m < 35 & 35 \le m < 60 \\ \hline \text{Frequency} & 15 & 25 & 24 & 11 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the frequency density for each class interval.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: On a histogram drawn on graph paper, the bar representing the class $10 \le m < 20$ has a width of $2\text{ cm}$ and a height of $7.5\text{ cm}$. Find the width and height of the bar representing the class $35 \le m < 60$.

questions.prompt:
The table gives the cumulative frequencies for the weights $w$, in kilograms, of 120 sheep at a livestock market:
$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Weight } (w\text{ kg}) & w < 30 & w < 45 & w < 55 & w < 70 & w < 90 \\ \hline \text{Cumulative frequency} & 0 & 24 & 64 & 100 & 120 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the class boundaries and calculate the frequency density for each of the four class intervals.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Assuming that the weights are evenly distributed within each class, estimate the number of sheep with weights between $50\text{ kg}$ and $65\text{ kg}$.

questions.prompt:
An environmental scientist monitors the daily concentrations of nitrogen dioxide, in $\mu\text{g m}^{-3}$, across 140 days in an urban area. The grouped data is shown below:
$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Concentration } (c\text{ }\mu\text{g m}^{-3}) & 20 \le c < 40 & 40 \le c < 55 & 55 \le c < 75 & 75 \le c < 105 \\ \hline \text{Frequency} & 28 & 42 & 46 & 24 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the frequency density for each class interval.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: On a histogram, the bar representing the class $40 \le c < 55$ has a width of $4.5\text{ cm}$ and a height of $8.4\text{ cm}$. Calculate the width and height of the bar representing the class $75 \le c < 105$, and find the total area on the paper, in $\text{cm}^2$, occupied by all four bars.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Air quality regulations stipulate that concentrations of $65\text{ }\mu\text{g m}^{-3}$ or greater are classified as high pollution. Assuming values are uniformly distributed within each class, estimate the percentage of days classified as high pollution.

questions.prompt:
The histogram below represents the masses $m$, in grams, of 142 metal ingots.
There are four touching bars with the following properties:
- Class 1: from 20 to 35 grams, height $d_1$
- Class 2: from 35 to 45 grams, height $d_2$
- Class 3: from 45 to 60 grams, height $d_3$
- Class 4: from 60 to 90 grams, height $d_4$
It is given that $d_2 = 2 d_1$, $d_3 = 3.2$, and $d_4 = 0.8$. The total number of ingots with mass less than $45\text{ g}$ is 70.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the values of $d_1$ and $d_2$, and find the frequency in each of the first two classes.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the frequencies in Class 3 and Class 4, and verify that the total frequency of all four classes is 142 ingots.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Estimate the median mass and the interquartile range of the 142 ingots, assuming values are uniformly distributed within each class interval.
